international.title: Politics live: Chalmers says economy faces ‘serious moment’ amid inflation; NSW ‘scaling up’ response after fire ants found in Sydney
international.summary: Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Wells says AI investment and creative protections not a ‘zero-sum game’ Weighing into the gigantic debate that is AI companies wanting to scrape Australian data to train models versus creatives who want to protect their work, Anika Wells says it’s not a ‘zero-sum’ game. I reject this sort of zero-sum game where building Australian sovereignty in AI must come at the expense of creatives or at diminishing the rights of creatives. At the moment, yes, we want deals, but we want creatives paid properly for their work. And the situation that we find ourselves in at the moment is that they’re not. They have no control and often no payment for their work. Continue reading...
